headline: US Labor Day: NYSE, Nasdaq and bond market closed; equity index futures on modified hours - Asia leads risk-on into Tuesday US reopen
summary: Both the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq are fully closed Monday for Labor Day, with no regular equity session or standard extended-hours trading. SIFMA-recommended bond markets are also closed. CME equity-index futures (ES/NQ) trade under modified holiday hours only. Setup for Tuesday US reopen is constructive: Asia posted a broad tech-led rally overnight (KOSPI +4.61%, Nikkei +2.12%) after Friday's US session finished mixed on the hot NFP print (S&P -0.05%, Nasdaq +0.09%, Dow -300, R2K -1.4%). US 10Y last at 4.79%, 2Y at 4.37%; CME FedWatch September hike probability holds ~60-65% into the Sept 15-16 FOMC. Key US catalysts this week: Oracle Q1 FY27 earnings Wednesday Sept 10 pre-open, TSMC August monthly revenue release Sept 10, August CPI Wednesday Sept 10 pre-open. Low-liquidity Monday: portfolio positioning risk skewed to Tuesday gap-open on Asia read-through.
source_name: Yahoo Finance / SIFMA (Labor Day 2026 market schedule)

headline: Asia session Monday: KOSPI +4.61% blowout to 6,995 on Samsung/SK Hynix HBM squeeze; Nikkei +2.12% to 66,400; Hang Seng -0.93% as China lags
summary: Korean market posted its largest single-day gain in weeks Monday: KOSPI closed +4.61% at 6,995.39, driven by parabolic moves in Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK Hynix (000660.KS) on confirmed HBM-supply drought (see separate entry). Nikkei 225 also strong, +2.12% at 66,399.84 - fresh all-time high - as advantest, tokyo electron and softbank tracked the memory rally. Hang Seng bucked the trend, -0.93% at 25,413.12, on continued China property drag and softer-than-expected August trade data (exports +4.9% YoY vs +6.0% consensus). Read-through into Tuesday US open: strongly positive for MU (US-domiciled HBM3E/HBM4 beneficiary of Korean squeeze), NVDA (HBM is Vera Rubin gating input), AMD (MI400 series), and equipment (AMAT/LRCX/KLAC/8035.T - Tokyo Electron cited by KOSPI leadership as capex expansion beneficiary). Moderately positive for TSM (Taiwan closed for typhoon; ADR read-through pending). Neutral-to-negative for Hang Seng-heavy names as China deceleration re-appears in the tape.

headline: KB Securities: Samsung and SK Hynix DRAM inventory drops below 10 days as HBM4 devours 3x wafer capacity; HBM export prices $76.13/unit (+9.5% MoM)
summary: KB Securities Monday morning report flagged that both Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have seen finished DRAM inventory drop below 10 days of shipments - a decade-plus low for the industry. Root cause: HBM4 mass production, in ramp since February at Samsung and June at SK Hynix, consumes approximately 3x conventional DRAM wafer capacity per bit, effectively removing supply from the general DRAM pool as fast as demand builds. Korea International Trade Association data shows HBM average export price per unit at $76.13 as of end-July, up 9.5% month-over-month and above $70 for the first time; QoQ price gain in Q2 was ~47%. All three vendors (Samsung/SK Hynix/Micron) have sold out 2026 HBM capacity and are >90% booked for 2027. Direct beneficiaries: 005930.KS (Samsung re-rating with HBM4 volume validated), 000660.KS (SK Hynix - absolute HBM revenue growing even as share compresses), MU (Micron - US-domiciled tightness beneficiary; earnings Sept 30). Second-order: NVDA (Vera Rubin bill-of-materials elasticity), AMAT / LRCX / KLAC / 8035.T (Tokyo Electron) on the capacity race to add ~50% by Samsung and >4x prior plan by SK Hynix. Watch for spot DRAM price spike this week as channel checks confirm.

headline: Anthropic to file IPO prospectus late September; potential ~$2T valuation; Q2 revenue $10.9B, first-ever operating profit ~$559M - largest AI listing test
summary: Multiple Sunday-evening reports converged on Anthropic's IPO timing: the company plans to file its S-1 prospectus with the SEC in late September (after post-Labor Day quiet period), begin marketing no earlier than mid-October, with listing targeted a few days before US midterm elections in early November. Investors have discussed a valuation as high as $2 trillion, with reported target raise of at least $130 billion - which would make it the largest IPO in market history. Financial disclosures via analyst leaks: Q2 2026 revenue $10.9B (up from $4.8B Q1 - a doubling), first-ever operating profit of approximately $559M. Anthropic also finalizing a $15B revolving credit facility. Read-through: massively positive for AVGO (Hock Tan disclosed on Sept 2 earnings call that Anthropic becomes AVGO's largest XPU customer in 2027 at >1GW Ironwood scaling to 3-4GW), positive for GOOGL (TPU supply relationship and Anthropic minority stake), positive for AMZN (multi-billion prior investments and Trainium exposure), and infrastructure providers CRWV, ORCL, DLR, EQIX, and power beneficiaries CEG, VST, GEV, ETN. Also validates the 'custom-ASIC concentration risk' narrative flip that Hock Tan defended on the Sept 2 call. Multiple sell-side desks expected to publish IPO-preview notes this week.
source_name: Motley Fool / Calcalist / TradingKey (Anthropic IPO timing Sept 6-7)

headline: Oracle Q1 FY27 earnings Wednesday Sept 10 pre-open: Street $19.13B / $1.30 EPS; focus on OCI growth (>92% guide) and $638B RPO conversion cadence
summary: Oracle (ORCL) reports Q1 fiscal 2027 Wednesday Sept 10 before the US market open. Consensus: revenue $19.13B, EPS $1.30. Bloomberg analyst forecast has OCI (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure) revenue climbing 92% YoY in the fiscal Q1, versus 52% a year earlier. Management guided prior for cloud order growth of 58-64% YoY. Investor focus areas: (1) trajectory of the $638B remaining performance obligation (RPO) into realized revenue - this is the single most-watched metric of the print given Wall Street's OCI-scale skepticism; (2) any color on OpenAI Stargate contract cadence and $500B multi-year framework announced last year; (3) capex trajectory - prior guide $25B+ FY27, watch for step-up; (4) commentary on HPE 'significant expansion' of gigawatt-scale AI collaboration flagged on the Sept 3 HPE call. Shares compressing below $149 into the print per technical setup. Positive earnings read-through would be constructive for CRWV (compute peer), NVDA (Stargate GPU pull-through), GEV (gas turbine backlog for Oracle datacenters), CEG/VST (Oracle nuclear PPAs are next logical shoe to drop). ORCL had gapped +36% in June on the OCI reacceleration print; setup for asymmetric move remains elevated.
source_name: Investing.com / ERP Today (Oracle Q1 FY27 preview)

headline: TSMC August 2026 monthly revenue release scheduled Wednesday Sept 10 - after July's +45% YoY print; N3/N2/A16 utilization the key marginal signal
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) publishes August 2026 monthly revenue Wednesday Sept 10 at Taipei market close (approx 3-5 AM ET). July's release printed +45% YoY - a re-acceleration versus H1 average - driven by AI accelerator pull-through (NVDA Blackwell/Blackwell Ultra volume, plus AVGO/GOOGL TPU/Anthropic Ironwood ramps). Watch: any commentary on N3E vs N2 mix (Vera Rubin and MI400 gating on N2 wafer allocation), Arizona fab utilization following the $100B additional investment announcement, and September-forward guidance implied by the print. CEO C.C. Wei publicly reiterated last week that AI-driven demand is 'robust through 2029-2030' with Nvidia now confirmed as TSMC's largest customer for FY2025. Positive read-through to any print >+40% YoY: NVDA, AVGO, AMD, MRVL (all N2/A16 anchor customers), plus WFE cohort (ASML/AMAT/LRCX/KLAC) on capacity extension implication. Monthly print is a leading indicator for the Oct 15 formal Q3 earnings.
source_name: TSMC Investor Relations / SEC 6-K filing calendar

headline: Constellation adds Walmart 176 MW nuclear PPA (Dresden Clean Energy Center) as CEG announces 920 MW Q3 signed - hyperscaler + Fortune-50 corporate demand converging
summary: Constellation Energy (CEG) disclosed 920 MW of new PPA signings in Q3 2026, headlined by a fresh Walmart 176 MW deal for the Dresden Clean Energy Center (Illinois) structured as two staggered 15-year terms beginning 2029 and 2030. This adds to the 20-year Microsoft PPA to restart Three Mile Island / Crane Energy Center (cleared major FERC waiver hurdle for grid-connection rights transfer earlier this year). Structural context: management guides adjusted EPS to compound at 20% annualized through 2029 off the $11.50-$12.50 FY26 base, and this projection excludes additional long-term contracts. Walmart signing widens the customer base beyond hyperscalers into Fortune-50 corporate PPA demand - broadens the addressable-market TAM materially and reduces hyperscaler concentration risk. Read-through: positive for CEG (fresh contract flow validates thesis; stock under pressure from PCG-downgrade / long-duration rate-back-up narrative Thursday), also positive for VST (Meta 2,600 MW PPA at Perry/Davis-Besse/Beaver Valley), and NEE / AES on the broader corporate-PPA read. Also read-through positive for SMR / OKLO as the corporate-PPA precedent extends demand-side runway for SMR technology deployments 2028-2032.
source_name: Motley Fool / Yahoo Finance (Constellation Walmart PPA)

headline: Blue Owl to launch publicly traded datacenter REIT; G42 (UAE) weighs US ownership structure to safeguard AI chip access - infra capital formation accelerates
summary: Two structural capital-formation items landed over the weekend that reinforce the datacenter-infrastructure thesis. (1) Blue Owl Capital disclosed plans to spin/list a publicly traded datacenter REIT, materially expanding the vehicle universe for institutional AI-infrastructure exposure beyond EQIX / DLR / CRWV. Blue Owl's existing datacenter portfolio (via IPI Partners acquisition) totals >$40B GAV. Read-through: positive for private-market datacenter valuations resetting higher (comparable pool grows); modestly negative for EQIX/DLR relative-value case as new supply of tradable REIT beta arrives. (2) G42, the Abu Dhabi AI conglomerate, is weighing bringing in US majority ownership to safeguard access to advanced US-origin AI chips under the Commerce Department case-by-case export review framework (Jan 2026 final rule). If executed, this restructures Middle East AI infrastructure demand pipeline - directly relevant to NVDA H200/Blackwell shipments to UAE and Saudi Humain, and to CRWV / ORCL Middle East DC leasing pipelines. Also validates ongoing US-policy tightening trajectory on end-user attribution.
